This may be one of my favorite games. From the excellent characters to the story and the player driven vibe, this is a great game. I've played the original fallout games and fallout 3 and 4, and while each has its merits, this is the one I return to. I've played this on crappy laptops with the lowest graphics and it runs well and looks good. I have a feeling you can complete this game in twenty hours, and maybe I did on one of my saves, but everything invites me to keep playing and explore every last inch of the map. Another huge bonus is the dlc. You don't need the gun runners aresenal-though it is nice, but the other dlc are fantastic. My only gripe is that you cannot return to complete these once you've completed the main quest. The game ends and you can either play your previous save or start over. I'd love to finish the game and then continue onto the dlc with the level boost and the perks. However for me this is a small complaint. I'll probably rack up another hundred hours on my new computer with this game and I'm excited.

tl;dr play this game and get the dlc

Incredible. The choice making and player freedom is unlike most modern RPG's as well as the other entries into the series. High replay value, and so much so discover, explore, and do in the Mojave and Vegas. Can't recommend this game enough, and it's a steal at only $11. The only issues with this game is the slight lack of quests that ask morally gray questions, and that once you have chosen a faction to side with, the game becomes somewhat linear although still very enjoyable and interesting. There are a few minor bugs that will cause the game to crash, but that's par for the course when it comes to games published by Bethesda.
Despite it's flaws, Fallout New Vegas is an amazing game, that is well worth the money.

Very fun for various kinds of players. Works well as an FPS but much better as an RPG. With the offical DLCs, it gives more than just more hours of gameplay and caters to various moods: Old World Blues being the more humourous I find. Still, as a Bethesda-developed game, I would recommend it for modders. The G.E.C.K. is much like the CS for Oblivion and Morrowind and allows a hell of a lot of freedom for modders to get carried away in. Good for those who want a quick play through, or those who like to emerse themselves in a fantasy setting. Only downsides (outside individual taste) are those you can expect with other Bethesda titles; the scale of the free-roaming maps and numerous side quests means there are little bugs and glitches here and there, though most are minor (e.g. rock floating a little off the ground) or have been patched in the most recent version of the game.

As a FO3 fan, I really loved FONV. In some ways it is different, but it's just like a FO3 with a different flavor. It has much more complexity regarding companions, and all the relations in-between many factions, which makes replay enjoyable, hardcore more for extra challenge.
I recommend getting all the DLCs, tho my favorite was Dead Money. Compared to DM others are not bad but under its shadow, yet all DLCs are a MUST play in my opinion have very unique atmosphere. you should drop all of your main items at you player home or somewhere safe and just go along with the gear you find in the DLCs.

You play as a Courier, on a mission to avenge themselves after being shot and robbed by the first antagonist of the game, Benny. Making your way across the Mojave desert, you soon learn the boundaries of where you can and can't go, and slowly experience contact with major and minor communities that dot the world. Reputation is introduced, where doing something wrong to a soon-to-be enemy will reward you with aggressive behavior in return. Slowly, running from town to town, you piece together the backstory and motive of Benny, and when you engage him, you learn that the package you carried isn't as innocent as it may seem.

Had this game for a while and never got around to playing it because I was turned off by the outdated graphics. Finally installed it and got playing and was immediately hooked. Ended up playing for 8 hours straight without even realizing an hour passed. The game does an incredible job selling the atmosphere and mood of the Mojave Desert in a post-nuclear-apocalypse setting, and you really start to care for the story once you get going. It starts right off, too. Not a whole lot of slow-paced exposition going on at the beginning, you can basically just start playing as soon as you get in. Love this game!

I'm rewriting this review in Febraury 2023. Thanks to some light modding, I am finally able to re-experience this game as I did the first when I played it over 10 years ago. I will admit the art and graphics have aged, but every other aspect of the game still holds up. The quests, the story, and the companions are all still the best the Fallout series has ever done. There is also still a vast amount of weapons and builds you can take your character. And then there is the icing on the already amazing cake: the DLC. The DLC for New Vegas sets the bar HIGH, and I am so happy I was able to replay it again this year. Thank you Obsidian and modders for making this one of the best games of all time.

One of the best RPGs ever made, done with an insane dedication by the original devs of Fallout 1 and 2. Sadly, they were faced with unfair corporate deadlines, so had to cut literally half of the game in order to make it in time, literally as they were polishing this half.

Hopefully cut content will be added back one way or another in the upcoming remaster/remake of Fallout: New Vegas, and I hope it will be done by Obsidian themselves.

Still it's an incredible game. A deserved cult classic. Give it a try.

Fallout New Vegas is a great game. In many respects, it is better than Fallout 3. It maintains a constant challenge throughout without being overly easy like post-level 20 Fallout 3. On the other hand, it is a bit stiff, and the map is empty in a lot of places. It's also quite glitchy. That being said, the writing is the best part of this game. You'll be on the edge of your seat at times.

To be compatible with new computers, it requires modes to work fluently and properly. Of course, you can still play even if you don't do anything. I also think that you will not need to evaluate the graphics in such an old game. As for my assessment, I think I have finished the story of the game 3-4 times, trying to make different choices each time. But I still know that there are completely different places, characters that I haven't seen, and tasks that I haven't done. The freedom offered to those who play is so good that I can't tell. I would like to say that besides the nuclear waste and hatred left over from the Old World, there is a game where you can do what you want without limits. Even if you have a slight interest in roleplay-style games, I recommend trying it out.

Fallout: New Vegas is still one of the best RPGs ever created. Even years later, very few games give you this level of freedom, choice, and consequence. Your decisions actually matter, the writing is sharp, the factions are memorable, and the world feels alive in a way that most modern games still struggle to match.

For how cheap this game often goes on sale, it’s honestly a steal. You’re getting dozens (if not hundreds) of hours of content, incredible DLC, and role-playing depth that puts many full-price titles to shame.

That said, the game does show its age. New Vegas can be buggy at times — occasional crashes, weird physics, or NPCs doing something unintentionally hilarious. Most of these issues come from how old the engine is, not poor design. With a few community patches or mods, the experience becomes much smoother.

Despite the occasional bugs, Fallout: New Vegas remains a masterpiece. If you enjoy meaningful choices, great storytelling, and immersive RPGs, this game is absolutely worth playing — especially at its current price. [10/10]
